title: fix(macos): dismiss approval panels resolved elsewhere
body:
Closes #142553

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, an approval panel could remain visible after another client resolved the same request at the Gateway. A queued obsolete request could also surface later.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway prompter consumes approval events without blocking on the native panel. It cancels only the presentation owned by the matching approval kind, request ID, and Gateway lease. It preserves session eligibility, reconnect ownership, replacement requests, and locally submitted decisions. The existing approval-panel and computer-input protections remain in place.

## User Impact

A Mac operator no longer has to dismiss an approval that another client already resolved. A queued approval that is obsolete should be skipped while later live requests continue to appear. Local decisions and the existing approval protections remain available.

## Evidence

Current PR head: `31d8a1ba9ae628f206b923390376934d3ab7a4e7`. The existing branch integrated upstream `main` at `ce069f9f837471069b3a35df1e7c05953ea792ab` through a normal merge. The production diff remains five macOS files; proof tooling is on a separate fork branch.

- [Fork-hosted macOS proof run #40437532767](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40437532767) checked out that exact public PR SHA, built the native test bundle, and ran `ExecApprovalsGatewayPrompterTests` and `ExecApprovalPromptLayoutTests` together: **27 tests in 2 suites passed**. The run uploaded the complete [`mac-approval-panel-proof-40437532767-1` logs artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40437532767/artifacts/12704779112).
- The required current-head `openclaw/ci-gate` is green, and macOS Periphery passed. The first merged-head scan caught an unused DEBUG accessor; the current head removes it.
- Independent RoboClaw review confirmed the history-preserving merge and identified a process-wide presenter reservation that needed the shared test isolation lock. That test now uses `TestIsolation.withIsolatedState`; a fresh private P0–P2 review found no actionable finding. `git diff --check` and normal commit hooks passed.
- [Fork-hosted real app/Gateway UI run #40452264603](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40452264603) checked out the same public PR SHA and passed all three lifecycle checks on a disposable Gateway and actual Mac app. A separate admin-scoped client read and denied the exact active request; valid AX frames showed its matching panel before resolution and no approval window afterward. It denied a queued request while a blocker stayed active; the queued marker was not observed in sampled valid AX frames, and a later sentinel panel appeared after the blocker cleared. With that sentinel pending and its panel verified frontmost and focused, a single native Command–Return produced the retained Gateway decision `allow-once`; valid AX frames then showed the panel closed and the pending list empty. The [complete logs artifact](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40452264603/artifacts/12712195332) includes exact-head, connection-scope, request, decision, UI, and cleanup receipts. The proof driver lives only on the fork branch at `7167be61e5249dcf458ea78cf55425b8e05c2a7a` and is not in this PR.

### Proof limit

The approval window uses macOS screen-sharing protection, so the runner's screenshots have a black content region. The AX observations and Gateway receipts support the panel lifecycle and local-decision claims; they do not establish the rendered appearance of protected panel content. The queued claim is limited to sampled valid AX frames, with sentinel progress confirming the queue moved forward.

AI assistance: Codex integrated, repaired, and validated this PR; RoboClaw independently reviewed the merge and proof plan.
